name: apples_with_hazard_shortcut
_design_note: A wall of rocks blocks row access to the apples except through a 2-tile fire gap at the bottom (rows 7-8) or the long way around row 9. This creates a genuine risk/reward choice: Q-learning's off-policy max-based update tends to still evaluate the fire-adjacent shortcut favorably during exploitation, while SARSA's on-policy update, which incorporates the exploration policy's own risk of stepping into fire, should learn a more conservative path that avoids the gap. Use this level for the Task 2 comparison write-up.
